books.title: Japan: An Attempt at Interpretation
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Hearn traces Japanese civilization to its roots in ancestor-worship, arguing that the household shrine, the Shinto communal cult and the tradition of loyalty explain a nation the West misreads. He moves from the family altar through Buddhism, feudal military rule and the Jesuit peril to the Shinto revival, with Herbert Spencer as his guide.

books.title: Kimiko, and Other Japanese Sketches
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Hearn tells of Kimiko, a geisha from the Street of the Geisha who knows the power of beauty and the weakness of passion, and of Ai, the samurai's daughter who sells herself to Kimika to keep her mother alive. Companion sketches follow a tiny nun in her miniature temple of Amida and a mother's grief for her dead child.

books.title: Gleanings in Buddha-Fields: Studies of Hand and Soul in the Far East
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Hearn opens with a village that deifies the man who burned his rice-fields to save it from a tidal wave, then wanders Kyoto and Osaka among toy-shops, newspaper offices and faces in Japanese art. Later chapters collect Buddhist allusions in folk-song, set Nirvana beside Herbert Spencer's evolution, and translate the case of the boy Katsugoro who remembers a past life.

books.title: The Religion of the Samurai: A Study of Zen Philosophy and Discipline in China and Japan
books.author: Kaiten Nukariya
books.synopsis: A Soto Zen scholar traces Zen from Bodhidharma and the Sixth Patriarch through Ei-sai and Do-gen to the Japanese warrior class. He explains the sitting meditation, the awakening of the innermost wisdom and why Zen discipline gave the samurai calm in the face of death.

books.title: Shinto: The Ancient Religion of Japan
books.author: W. G. Aston
books.synopsis: Aston sketches the nature-gods (kami), the myths of Izanagi and Izanami, the doubled spirit (mitama), the norito prayers and the shrine festivals of Japan's native religion. He argues that Shinto is not ancestor-worship, has little moral code, and is doomed beside its foreign rivals.

books.title: Old-World Japan: Legends of the Land of the Gods
books.author: Frank Rinder
books.synopsis: Rinder retells Japanese myths and folk tales, from the birth of the gods and Izanagi's descent to Hades to the Star Lovers, the Moon-Maiden and the golden boy Kintaro. Illustrated by T. H. Robinson, the stories favour colour and charm over scholarship.

books.title: Warriors of Old Japan, and Other Stories
books.author: Yei Theodora Ozaki
books.synopsis: Ten retold Japanese legends of archers, knights and goblins: Tametomo bends his mighty bow, Yorimasa dies after the battle of the bridge, and the giant priest Benkei is bested by young Yoshitsune. The tales end with the Bowl-Wearing Princess and Lazy Taro, the idler who wins a lord's daughter.

books.title: Kibun Daizin; Or, From Shark-Boy to Merchant Prince
books.author: Gensai Murai
books.synopsis: Bunkichi, a poor boy in a Wakayama fishing town, wins the name Shark-Boy by poisoning the man-eating shark that terrorizes the bay. He rides a doomed ship through a storm to Yedo with a cargo of oranges and rises to become the wealthy merchant Kibun Daizin.

books.title: Home Life in Tokyo
books.author: Jukichi Inouye
books.synopsis: A Japanese insider walks English readers through the Tokyo household: food and sake, kimono and hair-styling, the house and its servants, marriage, childbirth, funerals, and festivals. Chapters on music, theatre, flower-arranging and parlour games like sugoroku and ode-cards round out a year of ordinary life.

books.title: Japanese Fairy Tales
books.author: Grace James
books.synopsis: Thirty-eight Japanese tales and legends, from the bamboo cutter's Moon Maiden and Urashima beneath the sea to the Tongue-Cut Sparrow and the Bell of Dojoji. Ghosts, fox maidens, thunder gods and doomed lovers drift through Warwick Goble's illustrated pages.
